subject: Regional routing advisory: temporary reroute and post-incident actions (US/EU/APAC)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Corp IT <it@acme.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Immediate: service impact observed in multiple regions & temporary reroute

Hi team —

We observed a regional cloud networking degradation affecting inference traffic originating from US, EU and APAC zones beginning ~08:45 UTC this morning. Our serving runtime flagged elevated connection errors and increased tail latency for a subset of requests routed through the affected fabric.

What we did immediately:
- Switched routing policy to fail open for eligible customers and initiated cross-region reroute to healthy clusters (primary->secondary per account routing map).
- Enabled short-term aggressive prefix caching for warm connections to reduce KV lookups and mitigate tokenization retries.
- Opened a vendor incident with AWS (see AWS IR thread below).

Impact to Acme Corp:
- Short (~3–12 minute) spikes of 5xx and latencies up to 3x for some requests.
- Most traffic was successfully rerouted; a small percentage (~4%) of long-running streams experienced interruption and needed client retries.

Immediate ask for Acme:
- If you have region-locked endpoints, please confirm whether we can temporarily accept cross-region routing for the critical endpoints we discussed last quarter.
- If you need lower DNS TTLs or guidance on client-side retry windows, we can provide suggested settings in the next 30 minutes.

Attachments: preliminary_routing_map.png (visual of active reroutes)

We will follow up with a concise post-incident timeline and a proposed credit/compensation for any sustained errors. I will keep this thread for customer-facing updates; internal coordination will continue on the separate thread.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: AWS Incident Response <aws-ir@amazon.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:45:12 -0800
Subject: RE: Immediate: service impact observed in multiple regions & temporary reroute

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up. We observed increased packet drops on the inter-AZ fabric in eu-west-1 and partial BGP flapping that correlated with the traffic windows you reported. Our networking teams rotated fabric controllers and applied a targeted route dampening configuration at 09:18 UTC which has reduced the majority of flaps.

Current status:
- Mitigation applied; majority of control-plane instability resolved as of 09:20 UTC.
- We are continuing to monitor and expect stabilization across the affected zones within the next 2–4 hours.
- We opened internal case AWS-IR-2026-11-27-0893 (private).

We'll provide a formal AWS RCA when available; for now the recommended action is to keep your cross-region reroute in place until we have full stability.

Regards,
AWS Incident Response
aws-ir@amazon.com
From: Acme Corp IT <it@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Immediate: service impact observed in multiple regions & temporary reroute

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick response and the reroute. We saw a number of retries surface in our logs between 08:50–09:05 UTC and a couple of truncated streaming responses from your service around 08:58 UTC. Those streams are part of a regulated workflow (EU data residency requirement) — cross-region routing is allowed for retries but only for <15 minutes per incident per our SLA; anything longer requires written approval.

Can you share:
- An event-level timeline for the requests impacted (request IDs attached in the ticket).
- The justification and expected duration for the reroute.
- Confirmation of whether any customer data was persisted in a non-EU cluster during the reroute window.

We have opened a support ticket (ACME-SUP-6374) to track billing/credit questions. Please escalate if you believe additional credits are warranted.

— Priya Narayanan
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: customer follow-up plan and postmortem owners (Acme)

Team —

Summary of immediate asks from Acme (per their latest): event-level timeline, duration of reroute, confirmation on data residency, and potential credit. Proposed owner assignments:
- Event timeline & logs: Rafael Mendes (SRE) — compile trace-level evidence and map to customer request IDs.
- Data residency confirmation: Lauren Bishop (Legal/Privacy) — confirm whether any persisted state landed outside EU and draft the compliance note.
- Credit recommendation & commercial note: Marissa Cole (CS) & Hannah Schmitt (Sales Ops) — propose remediation credit tied to SLA and customer impact.
- External comms / RCA delivery: Marissa to lead the customer-facing RCA; scheduling 48 hours from now unless Acme requests earlier.

Attachments: reroute_playbook_v1.pdf (internal playbook used for today's cross-region reroute)

Checklist for the next 24 hrs:
1) Rafael — provide event timeline + raw logs by EOD PST today.
2) Lauren — confirm residency/no-persist by EOD. If persistence occurred, scope and duration.
3) Marissa/Hannah — draft customer-facing RCA and proposed service credit by tomorrow morning.
4) Schedule a 30-minute RCA meeting (propose Mon 30 Nov 10:00 UTC) and share calendar invite once timeline confirmed.

Keep responses in this thread for the customer record where appropriate; use internal channel for detailed debug artifacts.

Thanks,
Hannah
VP, Customer Reliability
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Corp IT <it@acme.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:35:00 -0800
Subject: Post-incident update and next steps (Acme) — incident 20261127

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for your patience. Quick consolidated update and next steps: 

What happened (short):
- 08:45–09:20 UTC on 2026-11-27 we observed control-plane instability in the cloud provider fabric that manifested as intermittent packet drops and route flaps. This led to short-lived 5xxs and a small set of truncated streams for a portion of your traffic.

What we did:
- Immediately switched to our documented cross-region reroute policy for eligible traffic and shortened client retry windows to reduce duplicate processing. We attached the internal reroute_playbook_v1.pdf we used.
- Coordinated with AWS Incident Response; they applied route dampening and controller rotations.

Findings (preliminary):
- No evidence that persistent customer data was written to non-EU clusters. Lauren confirms (cc'd) that there were no backend writes outside the EU.
- The majority of impacted requests were retried successfully; an estimated 4% of long-running streams saw interruption and required client retry.

Next steps for our teams:
- Rafael will share the per-request timeline and logs in the internal runbook link (private link) by EOD PST tonight.
- We propose a one-time service credit of 5% for the billing period covering the incident window; Hannah and I will finalize the commercial language and apply the credit once approved.
- Proposed RCA meeting: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 at 10:00 UTC. Please confirm availability; we will send a calendar invite.

Actionable items for Acme:
- Confirm whether the proposed 48-hour window for the RCA meeting works.
- If you require a formal data processing addendum update for cross-region temporary routing, please flag and we will escalate to Legal.

Postmortem doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/incident-20261127-postmortem (draft).

Attachments: reroute_playbook_v1.pdf, preliminary_routing_map.png

We will keep this thread updated and follow with final RCA and credits once all internal confirmations are complete.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
